svg.title: One Cohort, Five Observable Conversion Steps
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-02-qualified-buyer-cohort; chart type: funnel; title: One Cohort, Five Observable Conversion Steps; subtitle: Track qualified demand before increasing noncancelable capacity.; chapter number: 6; epistemic tag: illustrative_model; assumptions note: Illustrative 90-day acquisition cohort, not a revenue forecast. Every stage is a subset of the preceding stage; all counts represent buyer organizations rather than contacts or API keys.; caption: The cohort narrows 200 → 80 → 40 → 20 → 10. Sequential conversion is 40%, 50%, 50%, and 50%; overall conversion is 5%. Ten repeat buyers do not by themselves establish $675,000 billings.; stages: label: Documented prospects; value: 200 organizations with observable recurring capacity needs; numeric value: 200.0; detail: Build a named account list from permitted research and existing relationships. Record workload type, buyer role, current supplier arrangement, and likely purchasing window.; label: Qualified demand; value: 80 organizations with budget and technical fit; numeric value: 80.0; detail: Forty percent of the original cohort confirms budget, eligible destinations, expected usage, and acceptable retention terms during a documented discovery conversation.; label: Validated economics; value: 40 organizations pass workload and spread checks; numeric value: 40.0; detail: Half of qualified organizations supplies an authorized benchmark or traffic sample. Compare effective unit costs, p95 latency, retry burden, and minimum-commit exposure.; label: Funded pilots; value: 20 organizations prepay bounded production pilot balances; numeric value: 20.0; detail: Half of validated organizations accepts the service terms and funds a capped pilot. Record wallet liability separately from recognized revenue and enforce hard usage limits.; label: Repeat consumption; value: 10 organizations complete a second paid cycle; numeric value: 10.0; detail: Half of funded pilots consumes delivered service and purchases another cycle. Expand commitments only against observed repeat demand and customer concentration limits.

text.title: One Cohort, Five Observable Conversion Steps
text.tspan: One Cohort, Five Observable Conversion Steps

rect.title: label: Documented prospects; value: 200 organizations with observable recurring capacity needs; numeric value: 200.0; detail: Build a named account list from permitted research and existing relationships. Record workload type, buyer role, current supplier arrangement, and likely purchasing window.

label: Qualified demand; value: 80 organizations with budget and technical fit; numeric value: 80.0; detail: Forty percent of the original cohort confirms budget, eligible destinations, expected usage, and acceptable retention terms during a documented discovery conversation.

label: Validated economics; value: 40 organizations pass workload and spread checks; numeric value: 40.0; detail: Half of qualified organizations supplies an authorized benchmark or traffic sample. Compare effective unit costs, p95 latency, retry burden, and minimum-commit exposure.

label: Funded pilots; value: 20 organizations prepay bounded production pilot balances; numeric value: 20.0; detail: Half of validated organizations accepts the service terms and funds a capped pilot. Record wallet liability separately from recognized revenue and enforce hard usage limits.

label: Repeat consumption; value: 10 organizations complete a second paid cycle; numeric value: 10.0; detail: Half of funded pilots consumes delivered service and purchases another cycle. Expand commitments only against observed repeat demand and customer concentration limits.

text.title: Assumptions: Illustrative 90-day acquisition cohort, not a revenue forecast. Every stage is a subset of the preceding stage; all counts represent buyer organizations rather than contacts or API keys.
text.tspan: Assumptions: Illustrative 90-day acquisition cohort, not a revenue forecast. Every stage is a subset of the preceding stage; all
counts represent buyer organizations rather than contacts or API keys.
